messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Dedicated pool eu-west-1-pool-12 p99 latency > 3s for 5m. Affected route: /v1/chat/stream (hosted->dedicated fallback observed). Paging oncall.

maria: paging received, looking. Initial dashboard shows queue depth spike from 10 -> 450 in ~90s. p95 jumped 180ms -> 1.2s, p99 ~3.6s. Streaming stalls reported by a few customers (partial frames dropped). :fire:

ajay: on it. I can see a rapid warmup failure on new hotshot instances - handshake timeout to runtime and many requests queued waiting for KV cache load. Warmup avg time up to 22s vs expected 2s.

sam: any customer-visible errors? CS reports long tails for SparkDesk streaming sessions. They see partial responses and reconnects. No 5xx spikes currently, mostly higher latencies and stalls.

leo: looks like autoscaler attempted to add 4 nodes but they stayed in warmup state due to NFS mount delays and KV prefetch. Also saw node registration flapping for ~30s. Rolling back some warmup optimizations on the new image earlier today?

maria: confirmed deploy of runtime v1.12.3 at 06:12 UTC with warmup change. Could be related. Reverting is expensive; prefer mitigations first.

ajay: mitigation plan: 1) open handoff to oncall for live paging (increase priority). 2) temporarily route traffic to compatible smaller model variant on hosted tier for non-enterprise customers to reduce queue. 3) bump dedicated pool size via emergency capacity (if available) and force warmup of existing cold nodes with manual KV preload. 4) revert runtime warmup optimization if warmup remains >8s.

sam: routing change would need quick config toggle. I can flip route policy to preferential-hosted for model: redwood-chat-l1 where customer tolerance is acceptable. Will annotate which customers we can move.

natalie: CS: we'll notify SparkDesk about degraded streaming and offer retries. Which tenants are in pool-12? Send me list and estimated mitigation timelines so I can message them.

leo: running manual prefetch on 6 idle nodes now: command:

```
./infra-admin prefetch-kv --pool eu-west-1-pool-12 --model redwood-chat-1 --timeout 60s
```

Logs show prefetch success on 4/6 after NFS retries; 2 still pending due to mount I/O errors.

maria: action: escalate to infra-sre for NFS mount failures. ajay, can you confirm if we have alternative storage path? If not, we may need to reboot the two stuck nodes to force remount.

ajay: infra-sre looped in. Reboot queued for the two nodes that fail mount. ETA 4 minutes. Also increasing pool_min temporarily to allow allocator to bring up 3 extra nodes from standby capacity.

incident-bot: @oncall escalation: severity=sev2, impacted_customers=3, estimated_recovery=15-30m. Pager duty pinged: pagerduty-bot -> oncall group.

pagerduty-bot: @maria oncall acknowledged. Please provide byte-level mitigations and confirm rollback plan if warmup revert needed.

maria: confirmed. If manual mitigations fail in 20m: rollback plan is to revert runtime v1.12.3 warmup change to v1.12.2 and restart warmup watchers. That requires a coordinated config roll and will cause brief rebalancing.

sam: routing toggle applied at 06:38 UTC for non-enterprise routes -> immediate p95 improvement for those traffic by ~40%. Queue depth reduced by ~60 for pool-12.

leo: reboot completed for node-7 and node-9. Both remounted, prefetch completed. Node registration successful and joined pool. Seen immediate drop in queue and p99 down to ~1.4s.

natalie: notifying SparkDesk with current status: degradation, mitigations in progress, expected full recovery in 15-25m. They asked if dedicated customers can be moved; they accept temporary hosted routing.

ajay: monitoring. Next steps: keep autoscaler paused until we confirm warmup stability, run a verification job to simulate streaming tail load, and collect KV prefetch success rate over next 10 min.

maria: handing off to next oncall for continued watch and postmortem. Key items for postmortem: NFS mount flakiness, warmup optimization revert risk, autoscaler decision thresholds (how many queued requests trigger emergency capacity), and tenant routing rules for graceful fallback.

maria: @leo @ajay @sam @natalie please add any missing notes. I'll assign follow-up tickets and schedule a commander scrub in 48h.

leo: adding logs and timestamps to incident ticket now. Will include kernel mount errors and runtime warmup traces.

ajay: I'll draft a mitigation playbook entry: "Dedicated warmup failure -> emergency-hosted-fallback -> manual-prefetch -> node-reboot" and propose an autoscaler threshold change.

sam: thanks team. Moving channel to #incidents for postmortem artifacts. :white_check_mark:

maria: closing live mitigation phase. Leaving monitoring subscription open for 45m. Handoff complete.
